slides.title: Advertising Value *Equivalency*
slides.body: "This article would have cost $X as an ad." Easy to calculate, easy to inflate, and it says nothing about whether anyone changed their mind or bought anything.

slides.title: The 2025 Update Is *Blunter*
slides.body: AMEC's Barcelona Principles 4.0 say invalid measures such as AVEs **should not be used**. Measure outcomes and impact, not just outputs.

captions_meta.li_hook:
If your PR report leads with advertising value equivalency, it is measuring the wrong thing.
The industry framework has said so for years, and more bluntly in 2025.
li_body: AMEC's Barcelona Principles 3.0 (2020) state that "AVEs are not the value of communication". The 2025 update, Barcelona Principles 4.0, goes further: invalid measures such as AVEs should not be used.
A one-page report we recommend for SME and start-up teams:
li_points: The objective, agreed before the release went out.
Coverage by quality: target audience and tier, not just article count.
Key message pick-up: did the point you wanted actually appear?
One thing you will change next time.
captions_meta.li_close: What does your management actually ask for in a PR report?
captions_meta.fb: Your PR report probably doesn't need AVE. Here's a simpler one-page version that shows real value 👇
